parts.note: read literally, a plot that could blow up; historically, the 1605 scheme to blow up Parliament with barrels of a black explosive

explanation.surface: A warning about a scheme that could turn violent at any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive' looks figurative (a heated scandal) but is meant literally: Guy Fawkes's 1605 plot, remembered in Britain every 5 November with bonfires and fireworks.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1605 Catholic plan to blow up the Houses of Parliament with barrels of black blasting powder is the famous English conspiracy.

clue.text: It doesn't add much 23 on the subject

definitions.text: It doesn't add much 23 on the subject

parts.words: It doesn't add much 23 on the subject
parts.note: 23 is the answer to 23-across, a word for illumination; the clue describes a faint flicker that sheds very little of it

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about a contribution that barely clarifies a topic.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 23 gives the idiom 'shed light on the subject'; what adds only a little of it is a faint gleam, which also means a faint hint, as in a hint of hope.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint, wavering gleam gives only a tiny amount of illumination, just as a mere hint of understanding barely clarifies anything.

clue.text: No bird left this sum that's very small

parts.note: a mina (also spelt myna) is an Asian starling that can mimic speech

explanation.surface: Someone notes that with no birds left, the total has dwindled to almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This sum that's' merely links wordplay to definition; a nominal fee or sum is a token, very small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal charge is a token one, so tiny it exists in name only.

clue.text: Quick look at this form of art, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the art style is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Art Deco is the geometric 1920s-30s style, so the form of art is Deco

explanation.surface: An invitation to glance briefly at some artistic style.
explanation.walkthrough: DEKKO is British slang for a quick look ('have a dekko'), borrowed from Hindi via army use.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a glance, as in 'take a dekko at this'.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disordered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thespian has knocked over the cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges ACTOR and IT to make the soft Italian cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, fresh Italian whey cheese, one example of a cheese.

clue.text: 54 soldiers have disagreement about Italian name for city in Tuscany

definitions.text: Italian name for city in Tuscany

parts.note: 54 in Roman numerals is LIV (fifty, then four)
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
no is a word expressing disagreement

explanation.surface: A squad of fifty-four troops argues over what to call a Tuscan city.
explanation.walkthrough: The bare number looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but no 54 exists: it is Roman numerals. The port is known in English as Leghorn, hence 'Italian name'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan port Livorno is called Leghorn in older English usage, so its native Italian form is asked for.

definitions.meaning: to step up the pressure on someone, intensifying demands
literally, raise the temperature degree by degree, as by switching on a heater

explanation.surface: A tip on squeezing someone gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By degrees' looks like 'gradually'; it is the second definition, about thermometer degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to intensify pressure on someone, and literally means to raise the temperature of a room or oven.

indicators.note: entered means the word for one goes into the word for the carriage

parts.note: a pram is a baby carriage
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch climbed into a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a horse-drawn coach for a king, but it is a baby's pram.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend, Priam was the elderly ruler of Troy during the Trojan War.

parts.note: read literally, a 'drop out' from an aircraft: a leap from a plane with a canopy to slow the fall, not a quitter

explanation.surface: Someone who abandoned flying lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop-out' normally means someone who quits a course; here it is literally dropping out of an aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaping from an aircraft and descending under a canopy is literally dropping out during flight.

definitions.meaning: to arrange an insurance policy, getting protection against loss
to shelter or conceal oneself from danger

explanation.surface: Two words: protect your property, then conceal yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a noun (animal skin, or a birdwatcher's shelter), but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: One takes out cover to insure goods, and one shelters from fire or rain by getting under cover.

clue.text: Raven fluttering in soldiers' place of accommodation

indicators.note: in means the jumbled bird sits within the soldiers' letters

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

indicators.note: fluttering suggests wings beating chaotically, so the letters of the bird are jumbled

explanation.surface: A big black bird flapping about inside the barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluttering' turns RAVEN into AVERN, which goes 'in' TA (Territorial Army, the British reserve force). The definition is a Greek inn or restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek taverna is an inn or eating house, a place offering lodging or meals.

clue.text: Italian capitalist had nothing against dynasty

parts.note: a Roman lives in Italy's capital city, a play on capitalist
O looks like zero, meaning nothing
V is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: An Italian financier opposed a ruling family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitalist' suggests money, but means someone from the capital, Rome. 'had' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romanovs were the ruling house of Russia from 1613 until the 1917 revolution.

parts.note: a Canadian province shares its name with one of the Great Lakes, so its name also covers a stretch of water

explanation.surface: A question about whether a region of Canada is flooded.
explanation.walkthrough: The province of that name also names one of the five Great Lakes, so a part of Canada is quite literally covered in water.
explanation.definitionFit: A province of Canada and also one of the Great Lakes bordering it.

indicators.note: accepting means the man's name takes in the ring-shaped letter

parts.note: Carl is a man's name
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A suitor takes back an engagement ring from a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like jewellery; it is O. 'from' is a link before the definition, a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a lady.

indicators.note: rigged means fixed or tampered with, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a chubby candidate fixed the vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rigged' rearranges OUR and BALLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes someone plump and rotund, so round they might roll about.

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl
OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A young woman was found carrying a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like a cricket or police term; it means roped.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso an animal is to rope it, so lassoed means captured with a rope.

clue.text: Road not up to the mark?

definitions.meaning: a road running beneath another road or railway
read as two words, below a pass mark, failing an exam

explanation.surface: A highway that fails to meet the standard.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as UNDER PASS, it means failing to reach the pass mark in a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A road tunnelling beneath another route, and, split in two, scoring below the grade needed to succeed.

definitions.meaning: a person others walk all over, too submissive
the mat at the entrance on which one wipes one's feet

explanation.surface: A humble person who polishes boots.
explanation.walkthrough: Both meanings share the image of being trodden on.
explanation.definitionFit: A submissive person who lets others walk over them, and the mat at a front entrance on which people wipe their shoes.

clue.text: Game causing repetitive strain injury always inside

indicators.note: inside means the word for always goes within the injury's abbreviation

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A pastime that keeps giving players wrist injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' is a link word. Reversi is the board game of flipping discs, also called Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game in which players flip black-and-white discs to capture territory.

indicators.note: been removed suggests the letters are shifted out of place, so the remainder is rearranged
off means the letter for pound is taken away

parts.note: L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A black item whose price tag has been torn off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' takes L from LABELS, leaving ABELS, which 'been removed' rearranges. Sable is the heraldic word for black.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, sable is the term for the colour black.

definitions.note: read as 'colonist is', a singular noun

indicators.note: went round means the dog's letters encircle the letter for lake

parts.note: a setter is a gun dog
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A pioneer's hound circled a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonist's' reads as 'colonist is', the definition followed by a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is a person who makes a new home in a colony or new land.

clue.text: Linked Irish lady, no model, with daughter

indicators.note: no means the letter for model is dropped

parts.note: Bridget is a classic Irish woman's name, after St Brigid
Model T, the famous Ford car, gives T for model
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogy

explanation.surface: An Irish woman, not a fashion model, is connected with her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a fashion model; it is the Ford Model T, giving T.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridge two things is to span the gap between them, so bridged means joined.

clue.text: Developed remarkable love before edition five was included

indicators.note: was included means the numeral is put inside the combination
before places the jumbled word ahead of the edition abbreviation
remarkable here means notably changed, so the letters of the word for affection are rearranged

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A notable romance evolved before the fifth printing came out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' gives EVOL; 'was included' slips the five between that and the edition. 'Remarkable' suits the surface as praise of the romance, not a signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to develop gradually over time, so evolved means grown or advanced.

indicators.note: react can be read as re-act, act again differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting a wild Australian dog to respond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'react' rearranges DINGO, the Australian wild dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a task is carrying it out, just as making something is producing it.

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a route out, a line of exit

explanation.surface: Drawing up an escape route.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as OUT LINE, it means a route out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough draft or contour drawing, and, read as two words, a path for getting away.

parts.note: union here means marriage, not a trade union, so this describes someone single

explanation.surface: A worker who has not joined the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union; here it is the union of marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone single is not part of a wedded couple.

clue.text: More than the slightest bit pale?

indicators.note: bit means only a part of the word slightest is taken, the run sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A remark that something is a little more than faintly pallid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than the' links: the five letters are a 'bit' of SLIGHTEST, more than the minimal S.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale colour is a light shade, low in depth or intensity.

parts.note: in snooker each red ball sunk scores one point, so earning a single point means sinking that ball

explanation.surface: A snooker player scores a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a cue sport on a large table; the fifteen red balls are each worth one point when sunk in a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinking a red ball in snooker earns exactly one point.
